title: Widespread receptive field remapping in early primate visual cortex.
abstract: Predictive remapping of receptive fields (RFs) is thought to be one of the critical mechanisms for enforcing perceptual stability during eye movements. While RF remapping has been observed in several cortical areas, its role in early visual cortex and its consequences on the tuning properties of neurons have been poorly understood. Here, we track remapping RFs in hundreds of neurons from visual area V2 while subjects perform a cued saccade task. We find that remapping is widespread in area V2 across neurons from all recorded cortical layers and cell types. Furthermore, our results suggest that remapping RFs not only maintain but also transiently enhance their feature selectivity due to untuned suppression. Taken together, these findings shed light on the dynamics and prevalence of remapping in the early visual cortex, forcing us to revise current models of perceptual stability during saccadic eye movements.
